html:
At Morgarten, on 15 November 1315, men of Schwyz and Uri ambushed and routed a Habsburg army on a narrow road between a lake and a steep slope.

The army of Duke Leopold of Austria was marching to punish Schwyz in a quarrel over land and rights. The Swiss rolled stones and logs down the slope and attacked the trapped knights with halberds. Many were killed or drowned.

Weeks later the three valleys renewed their alliance. The victory showed that foot soldiers on their own ground could beat mounted knights, a lesson the Swiss repeated at Sempach in 1386 and in the Burgundian Wars. It made the Confederacy a power the Habsburgs could not easily crush.
sum: At Morgarten, on 15 November 1315, men of Schwyz and Uri ambushed and routed a Habsburg army on a narrow road between a lake and a steep slope.
